title: Retain removal of singleton Balanced first-pass fingerprint
question: Does omitting the count-pass digest reduce cost when both native singleton passes retain strict validation and independent row, header and metadata checks?
summary: The user-authorized source contract change reduced median elapsed 14.70% and median process CPU 18.40% across three verified 8 GiB pairs. Integrated within existing opt-in counted singleton Balanced and removed the temporary ablation flag.

workloads: 8 GiB repeated plain UTF-8, 8 equal consecutive parts, 1200 MiB actual cap, one worker, m256, hard 1 GiB/no swap.

validation.summary: Matched ablation controls and all output oracles passed. Final Linux formatting, default/all-feature lint/tests, WASM and WASI compile and release restore passed. Native Windows focused direct-run suite and default release passed.

limitations: Timed speed is for one repeated plain workload on WSL2/ext4.
An edit preserving decoded header, row count, byte length and mtime may go undetected.
Timing does not cover different codecs or native Windows.
exclusions: Small preflights, full warmup pair and first failed test assertion about the existing UTF-8 decoder wording.
reopen_when: Require platform/shape calibration before broader counted dispatch or further change to the source proof.
